prompt: Return paid revenue per account, including accounts with no paid orders.
rubric: Use a left join from accounts
Keep paid filtering in the join
schema:
accounts(account_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signup_date DATE, region TEXT)
sessions(session_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, started_at TIMESTAMPTZ, converted BOOLEAN)
orders(order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, ordered_at TIMESTAMPTZ, amount NUMERIC, status TEXT)
contacts(contact_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, contacted_at TIMESTAMPTZ, channel TEXT)
All timestamps are instants. Amount is order revenue. Use America/New_York for local-date questions. Use PostgreSQL. Unless stated otherwise, include only status = 'paid' orders; NULL amounts contribute zero revenue.
expectedQuery: SELECT a.account_id, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount),0) AS revenue FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.account_id=a.account_id AND o.status='paid' GROUP BY a.account_id;

expectedQuery: SELECT account_id, COALESCE(SUM(amount),0) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status='paid' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY revenue DESC, account_id LIMIT 3;
